title.value: A cognitive fingerprint in human random number generation
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper.
title.quote: A cognitive fingerprint in human random number generation

analysis.description: This study explores the uniqueness of human cognitive processes in random number generation. It investigates whether the process contains individual-specific patterns that can be identified through Damerau–Levenshtein edit distance. The study concludes that people have person-specific strategies in generating random numbers, forming a cognitive fingerprint.

type.justification: The study involves the examination of random number sequences from human participants, employing statistical methods and analyses to draw conclusions.
type.quote: We examined random number sequences of 115 healthy participants and developed a method to quantify the similarity between two number sequences.

name.justification: The study focuses on cognitive processes and brain function as they relate to random number generation.
name.quote: Is the cognitive process of random number generation implemented via person-specific strategies corresponding to highly individual random generation behaviour?

name.justification: The research investigates the cognitive strategies involved in random number generation and their individual variations.
name.quote: We address the general question of interindividual differences in the specific context of human random number generation and search for a cognitive fingerprint in random sequences.

name.justification: The paper explicitly mentions the usage of Python for statistical analyses.
name.quote: All statistical analyses were performed in Python.
